water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The only damage-type unit is an establishment-phase loss in Tunisia: drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in the governorate of Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This rests on a single ex-post review of project completion data and describes works that were never built, not damage to existing structures. Units about storage running dry or benefits shrinking in drought are effect units recording a benefit shortfall, not damage, and practitioner coping ratings are not counted here, so no unit in this row measures structural damage to built works.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, and WOCAT compilers judge pits, contour bunds, stone bunds and trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Most other compilers judge coping with rainstorms, thunderstorms, hailstorms or landslides as good or moderate, and those for terraces in Haiti, Thailand and Bangladesh and for marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan as very good [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm]. All units except the Loess Plateau evaluator observation are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, ripper tillage) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure. The Loess Plateau observation gives no measure of damage and ties the threat to repair funding and subsidies in adjacent areas as much as to exposure [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau with few local funds to repair it, and WOCAT compilers judge pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1139_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers in Tunisia, Eritrea, Kenya, Yemen, Uganda, India, Madagascar and Ethiopia judge coping as good, and those in Burkina Faso, Bangladesh and Somalia as moderate; the Haiti and Bangladesh terrace sheets judge coping with landslides as very good [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_landslide]. All units except the Loess Plateau observation are practitioner judgements without damage records, and for field-level practices a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with forest fire and well with land fire, and stone check walls and check dams in India as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from two technology sheets with no observed damage; earth and stone works offer little to burn, so any fire effect would fall on vegetation on or around them.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, check-dam failure releases stored sediment, large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen, banquettes lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. WOCAT compilers judge jessour in Tunisia, zaï pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, check dam ponds in Ethiopia, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with river or flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, check dams in Tunisia, China and India, and spate or water-spreading systems in Eritrea and Sudan to cope well, those for marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia to cope very well, and those for weirs in Ethiopia and works in Somalia to cope moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood]; these are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, tillage) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields to floodwater rather than damage to a structure. Literature failures are tied to maintenance and design: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. The sediment-release statement comes from a USA study and the Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements [ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: A review of terraces names torrential rain, together with the collapse of walls and vegetation strips and use after abandonment, among the conditions that degrade terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3]. WOCAT compilers judge a check dam for land in China and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde to cope well with river floods, and marab floodplain agriculture and mechanised Vallerani micro-catchments in Jordan to cope very well with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1455_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5860_2021_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The pool is small and, apart from the review, consists of practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets rather than measured damage; the review ties damage to abandonment as much as to rainfall. The Jordanian ratings carry no damage signal at all.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the technology as coping very well with extreme winter conditions [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating from Jordan with no observed damage, so it says little about frost exposure elsewhere [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rates the technology as coping moderately with heatwaves [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reason or observed damage, for a structure of stone and wire that heat would affect mainly through the vegetation around it [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, and Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: No unit describes how wind damages the works; the row rests on WOCAT compiler judgements of how terraces, bunds, pits, check dams, sand dams, spate systems and rooftop tanks cope with local windstorms and tropical storms. Most are judged to cope well, while progressive bench terraces in China and fascine vegetative check dams in Madagascar are judged not to cope well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets, not measurements; compilers for bench terraces in Bangladesh and gabion works in Somalia judge coping as moderate, and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso is judged to cope very well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1528_2012_local_windstorm]. For field-level practices such as pits and bunds a rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: In Burkina Faso the proximity of zai pits on bare, crusted land raises germination and seed dispersal, so herbaceous and woody species re-establish on formerly barren fields, and users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_roose93_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_zoug14_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_kabo04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. WOCAT compilers give a mechanism with each rating: water held by on-farm ponds in Cambodia lets plants grow, sand dams in Kenya rejuvenate riverine ecologies and enable indigenous tree planting, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia improve soil moisture, vegetation and habitat for livestock and small wildlife, and the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso brings more forage grasses, returning legumes and observed insects, birds, reptiles and mammals [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2844_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1537_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1528_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1528_2012_animal_diversity].
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: The WOCAT units are compiler ratings from documented technology sheets in Burkina Faso, Kenya, Cambodia, Somalia, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Zambia, not measurements, and several sheets supply separate plant, animal and habitat ratings; the literature units are descriptive species counts or user perceptions with no untreated comparison, and the zai counts partly restate the same earlier observation. The Magoye ripper sheet in Zambia rates animal diversity unchanged, the Bangladesh bench-terrace rating is an expectation for a planned cropping system, and the Bhutan rating refers to more diverse crops [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1139_2013_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4284_2018_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity].

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: Consecutive years of zai planting pits on formerly bare, barren soil in central Burkina Faso were followed by the re-establishment of herbaceous species and of trees and shrubs.
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: Both units are secondary citations of earlier zai field observations from Burkina Faso, probably overlapping, reporting species counts on treated land without an untreated comparison or a biodiversity index; the strength of the effect is not quantified.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: WOCAT compilers attribute carbon gains to more vegetation: the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso raises biomass production many times over nearby unploughed soil, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia increase biomass and, through vegetation recovery and sediment accumulation, soil organic matter, a haffir in Somalia allows vegetation cover to regenerate, gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan add below-ground organic matter through expanding roots, and the Magoye ripper in Zambia does so through less soil disturbance [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1528_2012_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7778_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7777_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1139_2013_biomass_above_ground_C]. Emission ratings rest on tree nurseries enabled by sand dams in Kenya and tree cover building up over time at a masonry check dam in Ethiopia, and in the literature zai fields in Burkina Faso treated for several years had higher organic matter while trenches combined with vegetation raised soil organic carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1537_2012_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_6716_2023_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Most units are compiler ratings from documented technology sheets in Niger, Uganda, Jordan, Tunisia, Sudan, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Haiti, Bangladesh, Bhutan and elsewhere, not measurements, many soil organic matter ratings carry no comment, and soil organic matter and emission ratings are proxies rather than measured sequestration; the Bangladesh emission rationale (crops absorbing more carbon dioxide under higher cropping intensity) is not long-term storage, and the Bhutan sheet describes organic matter moving downslope within each terrace [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_4284_2018_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6891_2023_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. The literature is mixed: trenches in Mexico lowered soil nitrogen and carbon, and a zai trial in Burkina Faso found no significant change in organic matter by the end of the experiment even though biomass rose [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose93_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In low-income settings the pathway is zai pits building soil organic matter over time, with organic matter and nitrogen higher on fields treated for several years.
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Both units are zai in Burkina Faso and measure soil organic matter, a proxy for carbon; one is a secondary citation of an earlier study and the other, a controlled trial, found no significant change in organic matter after two years.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for marab floodplain water harvesting and mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rate soil organic matter increased, and a review of infiltration trenches reports that trenches combined with vegetation raised soil nutrients including soil organic carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5770_2020_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5860_2021_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The Jordanian ratings carry no compiler comment and are practitioner judgements, not measurements, with soil organic matter standing in for sequestration. The same review reports that trenches in Mexico actually decreased soil nitrogen and carbon, so the in-scope literature is split [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: Pooled costs are the up-front works cost per hectare: treatment of sub-watersheds with soil and water conservation works in two India watershed projects, average investment cost of spate-irrigation systems in Yemen (of which farmers paid a share), and rehabilitation of pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru.
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The pool mixes different denominators and practices: watershed treatment cost per treated hectare in India (lender-evaluation figures), the per-hectare investment cost of spate irrigation systems in Yemen from a completion-report beneficiary survey, and a historical rehabilitation cost for Andean terraces in Peru, an upper-middle-income case. Currency years are not stated for most figures, and the India costs are described by the evaluator as high by national norms.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: Pooled units describe how siting and implementer affect what structures cost: in Karnataka, land-resource-inventory planning avoided unnecessary structures and lowered the construction cost of soil and water conservation works per hectare versus a conventional programme; in Ghana, the share of small dams rehabilitated below given per-irrigated-hectare cost thresholds differed between government and donor/NGO implementers.
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: Both are from lower-middle-income countries but measure different things: the India figure is an absolute construction cost per hectare from a lender completion report (the saving is relative to another SWC programme, not to no intervention), and the Ghana figure is a distribution of dam rehabilitation costs by implementer, not a cost reduction.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In-field practices (zaï and tassa pits, stone bunds and stone lines, terraces, tied furrows and conservation tillage) let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the root zone, so crops suffer less in dry spells and still yield in dry years: zaï produced sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. Storage works (domestic and production cisterns, sand dams, subsurface dams, ponds and check dams) carry water into the dry season for households, livestock and supplemental irrigation and reduce reliance on water trucks or tankers, and WOCAT compilers across sheets from Niger, Burkina Faso, Kenya, Ethiopia, Tunisia, Somalia, India and other countries rate soil moisture and water availability as improved and drought impacts as reduced [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1219_2014_soil_moisture, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_water_quantity, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings of soil moisture or water availability, which are practitioner judgements and component proxies for drought impact rather than measured losses; the measured and literature units show the benefit shrinking in severe drought, with stone bunds in Burkina Faso giving no gain in the driest year and Niger families with soil and water conservation moving from surplus in good years to deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1]. Storage is bounded (most of the Kenyan sand dams studied could not supply one household through the whole dry season), a meta-analysis found no significant soil-moisture effect of infiltration trenches, an Ethiopian watershed programme showed no difference in soil water retention, and a few WOCAT sheets rate water availability or soil moisture as unchanged [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1, ev_soil_water_retention_abate21_5, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1474_2011_soil_moisture]. Storage also fails in prolonged drought, with subsurface dams in Brazil drying out in a rainless year, domestic cisterns running dry in great multi-year droughts, and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limiting soil-conservation benefits; these units record no benefit rather than damage to the works, and several literature results are bundled programmes or implementer, Bank and Embrapa self-assessments [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the literature is mostly from semi-arid Brazil, where domestic and production cisterns, subsurface dams and runoff ponds used for supplemental irrigation store rain into the dry season, giving households basic drinking water, keeping livestock watered and reducing reliance on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. In-field tillage and terraces raise soil moisture, with broad bench terraces in semi-arid China holding up to 22% more moisture than vegetated slopes, and WOCAT compilers rate soil moisture as improved for terraces, check dams, conservation tillage and micro water harvesting in Peru, China, Thailand, the Philippines, South Africa and Jordan [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9, ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_2, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1506_2011_soil_moisture, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_5860_2021_soil_moisture, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_968_2011_soil_moisture].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Storage caps the benefit: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families used the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. Much of the Brazilian pool is implementer, Embrapa or agency assessment, interviews or census inference without a counterfactual, the WOCAT units are compiler ratings rather than measurements, and a meta-analysis of infiltration trenches found no significant soil-moisture effect [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1]. Subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells, and domestic cisterns run dry in great multi-year droughts; these units record no benefit (a benefit shortfall, not damage), and most other units measure soil moisture or water access as component proxies rather than drought losses [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Water harvesting buffers dry periods by storing or infiltrating water: zai pits reduce the impact of dry spells of a few weeks when soil water storage is sufficient, runoff ponds in semi-arid Brazil supply supplemental irrigation and production cisterns supply livestock water, cisterns in China are reported to mitigate frequent droughts, and public-works interventions in Ethiopia raised water availability. WOCAT compilers for Vallerani micro-catchments, ponds, check dams, terraces, stone lines and water-spreading weirs judge drought impacts reduced through stored water, infiltration and soil moisture retention, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought.
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Much of the pool is practitioner judgement from technology sheets or expert assertion (Brazilian research and programme authors, a lender evaluation in China without measurement), and only the Rwanda unit rests on a comparison against controls, reported second-hand in a completion report. The Ethiopian study notes vegetation greenness still tracked local drought severity, the Haiti compiler states the impact is not yet measured, and the zai effect depends on soil storage capacity. Storage itself runs short in prolonged drought: subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year, domestic cisterns run dry in great multi-year droughts, and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits; these units record no benefit at that point, a shortfall rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, water from runoff-harvesting ponds applied as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells has reduced crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall, and water stored in production cisterns can reduce livestock mortality in severe droughts [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Against this, subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year, small ones do not withstand long dry spells, and domestic cisterns run dry in great multi-year droughts so households fall back on water trucks; these units record no benefit when storage is exhausted, a shortfall rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3]. All units come from Brazilian research and programme authors, an upper-middle-income context adjacent to the target, and none gives a drought-impact metric.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Zai pits in Burkina Faso reduce the impact of dry spells of a few weeks when soil water storage is sufficient, cisterns in China are reported to mitigate frequent droughts, and public-works watershed interventions in Ethiopia improved drought resilience by raising water availability. WOCAT compilers for Vallerani micro-catchments, ponds, check dams, terraces, stone lines and water-spreading weirs judge drought impacts reduced through stored water, infiltration and soil moisture retention, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster.
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Most units are practitioner judgements or assertions without a drought metric, including a lender evaluation in China with no measurement; the Rwanda comparison against controls is reported second-hand in a completion report. In Ethiopia vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, and the Haiti compiler notes the impact has not yet been measured. In Tunisia, consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits, a unit recording no benefit rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__establish.mechanism: Establishment costs pooled here are the up-front costs of building or rehabilitating structures: soil and water conservation treatments per hectare in two India watershed projects, average investment cost per hectare of spate-irrigation systems in Yemen (with the farmer's share), and rehabilitation of Andean terraces in Peru.
water_harvesting_conservation__establish.conditionality: The pool mixes different denominators and practices: watershed treatment cost per treated hectare in India (lender-evaluation figures), the per-hectare investment cost of spate irrigation systems in Yemen from a completion-report beneficiary survey, and a historical rehabilitation cost for Andean terraces in Peru, an upper-middle-income case. Currency years are not stated for most figures, and the India costs are described by the evaluator as high by national norms.

water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.mechanism: The practices limit fire mainly by removing fuel: on intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little to spread on, and the Vallerani compiler in Burkina Faso keeps the treated area open to regulated grazing to cut the grass growth that could carry a fire, with herders also watching the area [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_fire_risk]. WOCAT compilers for bench terraces in Bangladesh and stone check walls and check dams in India also rate fire risk as reduced [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.conditionality: The terrace statement is an expert estimate that its authors say has no experimental basis on terraces, and the other units are WOCAT practitioner ratings, the Bangladesh and India ones without any stated reasoning [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1]. The effect depends on grazing or other management keeping biomass down rather than on the structures themselves.

water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.mechanism: Contour stone bunds and stone lines, bench and progressive terraces, infiltration trenches, check dams and micro-catchments slow and spread runoff on hillslopes: terraces cut mean runoff by 50 to 98% on small mountain plots and lowered flood peaks, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment cut runoff volume by 50% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2]. WOCAT compilers across sheets from Niger, Ethiopia, Tunisia, Rwanda, China, Somalia, Jordan and other countries rate surface runoff, soil loss and downstream flooding as reduced, the Kenyan sand-dam sheet noting that a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7778_2026_surface_runoff].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.conditionality: Nearly all units are runoff or soil-loss measures or WOCAT practitioner ratings standing in for flood impact at plot or small-catchment scale; catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, an Uttarakhand water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent, and Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by only 3.2 percent against conventional sites [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Diversion structures can work the other way: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled the runoff coefficient and raised peak discharges, larger sand dams increase flooding risk, and check dams can cause downstream channel incision [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1]. Among the ratings, the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates flood impacts as worse, the farm-pond and Nepal rooftop sheets rate downstream flooding as unchanged, and the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.mechanism: Terraces, contour stone bunds and lines, check dams, sand dams and water-spreading structures slow and spread runoff and retain water and sediment, lowering peak discharges and lengthening flood rise times; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50%, and WOCAT compilers for many of these structures judge downstream flooding reduced. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods, and spate and diversion structures in Yemen are said to control floods.
water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.conditionality: Most units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and catchment-scale measurement is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported. Direction depends on design: diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes raised peak flows, larger sand dams increase flooding risk, a conservation-tillage sheet from the Philippines rated flood impacts worse, and a farm pond in India and a rooftop system in Nepal were rated neutral.

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: A review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: This is one narrative statement from a review that does not name specific practices, does not separate heat shocks from low rainfall and gives no magnitude; no unit measures heat-stress losses directly [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Water harvesting and conservation structures capture runoff and raise soil moisture so rainfed crops yield more, especially in dry years and low-rainfall areas; stored water allows supplemental irrigation and extra crops, stone lines trap sediment and organic matter, and converting slopeland to levelled terraces increases moisture retention. In Burkina Faso stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% and by about 142% with compost, and WOCAT compilers across many technology sheets judge crop, fodder and animal production increased, citing moisture retention, regenerated grasses and better water access.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The pool mixes independent evaluations (matching studies in Ethiopia, a difference-in-difference evaluation in Rwanda) with lender self-reported completion-report figures, bundled watershed programmes that combined works with seed and crop-husbandry packages, and a large body of practitioner judgements from technology sheets. Nulls and negatives are present: conservation promoted mostly off-farm had no yield effect, late adopters and the pooled sample in Ethiopia showed no significant gain and benefits appeared only once structures were maintained for at least seven years, bunds lowered yields in high-rainfall Amhara, zai lowered sorghum yields under waterlogging in Cameroon, diversion banquettes in Niger cut yields, and keeping grazing animals off newly treated rangeland lowered animal production ratings in Niger; much of the zai gain rides on added manure or compost.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In semi-arid settings, pits (zai, tassa), stone bunds, tied furrows and subsurface dams concentrate scarce rainfall in the root zone or store it for later use, raising cereal yields and enabling harvests in drought years when untreated fields fail.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Evidence mixes Sahelian field results (Burkina Faso, Niger) with Embrapa and cistern-programme sources from semi-arid Brazil, several of them self-assessments or expert statements; the Brazilian programme effects are on value of production, a proxy, and some yield gains depend on manure added to the pits.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In rainfed hill and watershed systems, in-situ rainwater conservation, terracing and soil and water conservation works combined with crop packages raise yields: average rainfed crop yields rose 24% and 26% against controls in Karnataka watershed phases, rainfed crop productivity rose 20.8 percent by difference-in-difference in Uttarakhand, and maize on terraced Rwandan hillsides rose from 1.5 to 2.8 tons per hectare [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. The DIME evaluation reported for Rwanda found the value of harvests 36 percent higher than in the control group [ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Every unit is a bundled programme in which conservation works came with improved seed, vermicompost, crop packages or life-saving irrigation, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated, and all are drawn from Bank completion reports or IEG reviews of them [ev_crop_yield_hp17_2, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1]. The Rwanda maize figure is project monitoring before and after without a control, and the Uttarakhand terrace figure compares with- and without-project models [ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In the Brazilian semi-arid, subsurface dams, tied furrows, micro-catchments with rescue irrigation and production cisterns store or concentrate water, raising crop productivity, enabling extra harvests and expanding the value of family production; in the Andes, infiltration trenches raised yields on some plots.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Upper-middle-income evidence only, largely Embrapa and programme self-assessments plus one quasi-experimental study of value of production (a proxy); a trench review from Peru reports both positive and negative yield effects, and one cistern-programme author states there are no quantitative impact evaluations.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: Higher and more stable yields, irrigation of gardens and higher-value crops from stored water, and better fodder and livestock raise household income and food security; beneficiaries shift from staples to vegetables, and a quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_economic_return_mala24_1]. WOCAT compilers describe the same pathway: planting pits in Uganda keep banana stands fruiting through drought and raise harvests for sale, ripper tillage in Zambia gives better tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost, farm ponds in Cambodia supply irrigation during drought, and contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area for diverse crops [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1139_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Most pooled units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT technology sheets, and much of the literature comes from bundled watershed programmes and lender completion or appraisal reports, so measured household effects are a minority. Independent evaluations are more cautious: no significant effect on food security or total income in Ethiopian programmes, terraces reducing net crop income, a Brazilian cistern programme with a benefit-cost ratio far below break-even, single SWC measures not covering their annual costs, and sand dams likely not cost-efficient [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1, ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_economic_return_zoug14_3, ev_economic_return_ritc21_1]. Compilers also rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and record no change on several sheets, including a subsistence farm pond in India; Kenyan sand dams sit inside a wider food-security programme, and food security, income and returns are all proxies for poverty [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency].

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In semi-arid areas, cisterns and subsurface dams let families irrigate gardens and fruit, diversifying diets and raising farm income, while zai and stone bunds raise cereal output and return to labour; food security rises with the area of farm under bunds.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Income gains from the Brazilian cistern programme are small and turned negative for larger farms, its benefit-cost ratio is well below one, and subsurface dams yielded little cash income in stagnant local economies; a Sahelian study found SWC families still in deficit in low-rainfall years, and single SWC measures did not repay annual costs.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In the Brazilian semi-arid, cisterns and subsurface dams supply water for gardens, fruit and livestock, improving diets and raising family farm income, with the largest income effects on small farms; Andean terrace rehabilitation is judged to pay back through long durability.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Evidence is from upper-middle-income Brazil and Peru, outside the LIC/LMIC target band. A quasi-experimental study found modest income gains, no effect outside the Northeast, a negative effect on larger farms and a benefit-cost ratio far below one; several units are Embrapa or programme self-assessments and household self-reports.

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and lines, banquettes, trenches, pits and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers across many countries rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced, explaining that micro-catchments cut the kinetic energy of rain by trapping runoff and that check dams slow runoff so soil accumulates upstream [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_soil_loss].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: Over two thirds of the pool are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and several literature sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Indian sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies. Negative findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. Some sheets rate no change, including a rooftop system in Nepal, and the Zambian tillage sheet expects less downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Tunisia, drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The single unit comes from an ex-post review drawing on project completion data and describes an establishment-phase shortfall of works, not physical damage to structures already built.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Costs are the per-hectare unit cost of watershed treatments (bunds, check dams and other soil and water conservation works) across treated area in two World Bank-supported India watershed projects.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both figures come from one evaluation of bundled watershed programmes in India and are treatment costs per hectare treated, not per hectare of degraded land restored; the evaluator compares them with national budget norms rather than with outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Better-sited planning based on a land resource inventory avoided unnecessary structures, so construction of soil and water conservation works cost less per hectare than under the conventional integrated watershed programme.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single lender completion-report figure from Karnataka, India, in local currency at stated price terms; the comparison is against another watershed programme, so it shows a saving from planning rather than the cost of SWC versus no SWC.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: These are programme-scale packages of soil and water conservation and water-harvesting works. In India, participating villages cut tanker water transport by 56 percent against non-participating villages and Karnataka project watersheds had soil moisture 30.5 percent higher than conventional watershed sites; in Ethiopia the PSNP public works raised water availability and watershed drought resilience, and in semi-arid Brazil cisterns expanded rural water access and can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1, ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A review of quasi-experimental studies finds soil and water conservation methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a bundled programme or unspecified soil and water conservation, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Karnataka figure comes from a Bank completion report, and the Brazilian statements are a census-based inference without a counterfactual and a statement of potential [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. An independent Ethiopian evaluation found no significant difference in remote-sensed soil water retention between beneficiary and control watersheds, the PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and in Tunisia consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_soil_water_retention_abate21_5, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed works and production cisterns increase stored water, which improved watershed drought resilience in Ethiopia and can reduce livestock deaths in severe droughts in Brazil [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Ethiopian public-works study bundles area closures, small-scale irrigation and soil and water conservation, the Brazilian cistern statement is framed as a potential effect, and in Tunisia consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits (no benefit rather than damage); none quantifies drought impacts [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed programmes combining physical and vegetative barriers, bunds, check dams and terraces reduce runoff and soil loss: runoff dropped by 5 to 18 percent across Indian states, downstream runoff in the Karnataka catchments examined fell by 10 to 22 percent, and Ethiopian public works cut soil loss by 32.2% [ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_5, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_arega24_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are bundled programme results measuring runoff or soil loss as proxies for flood impact, several from Bank completion reports or perception surveys, such as 84 percent of Ethiopian respondents reporting reduced run-off [ev_runoff_reduction_eth16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Effects at watershed scale are small or absent: Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by 3.2 percent against conventional sites, Uttarakhand sediment yield fell only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year, and its water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent [ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is one narrative statement from a review that does not name specific practices, does not separate heat shocks from low rainfall and gives no magnitude; no unit measures heat-stress losses directly [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Soil and water conservation structures (terraces, bunds, check dams) retain moisture and soil, raising crop yields and value of production; the gains are larger in low-rainfall or climatically variable areas and in dry periods. Water harvesting with irrigation also lets households diversify crops.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most magnitudes are from bundled programmes or lender completion reports (Ethiopia public works, India watershed projects, Mauritania), with value-of-production and forage biomass used as proxies. Independent Ethiopian studies show effects only for early adopters and only after several years of maintained structures; SWC promoted off-farm, imposed structures, and bunds in high-rainfall areas showed no gain or losses.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed and SWC programmes raise household income through higher yields, irrigation and diversification, and watershed investments in India show modest positive returns across many case studies. A quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most magnitudes are from bundled programmes with weak attribution (IEG calls a China income estimate not robust and notes India income gains may partly be construction wages; a Karnataka ICR doubts its own before/after figures). Independent studies found no effect on food security or per capita income, household benefit-cost ratios mostly below one at market wages in Ethiopia, and a cistern programme benefit-cost ratio well below one in Brazil; income and food-security figures are proxies for poverty.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Nearly all units are programme or lender reports from Ethiopia, India and China, often perception surveys or before/after comparisons; an Uttarakhand water budget showed surface runoff slightly increasing, the Karnataka runoff comparison is against another SWC programme, and IEG doubts the India runoff measurements. Effects mixing runoff and soil-loss metrics are only components of erosion risk.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sediment-control dams, terraces and vegetation in a Loess Plateau watershed programme capture sediment each year, reducing the load reaching downstream rivers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single modelled programme-level estimate from a lender review in China, using sediment retention as a proxy for water quality.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed SWC and recharge structures raise water tables and spring discharge, enabling small-scale irrigation and reducing water transport by tanker in participating villages.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Mostly programme reports from India and Ethiopia without untreated comparison sites; IEG notes recharge gains may be wiped out by subsidised tube-well pumping, year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso, and the Uttarakhand recharge change is a small modelled water-budget figure.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for zaï or tassa planting pits and contour bunds in Niger, planting pits in Uganda and conservation tillage with the Magoye ripper in Zambia judge the technologies to cope well with drought [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1219_2014_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1652_2014_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1587_2013_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1139_2013_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets, not measurements, with no observed damage or failure data behind them. These are field-level practices, so the ratings describe how the treated fields fare under drought rather than damage to a built structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate zaï or tassa pits and contour bunds in Niger and ripper tillage in Zambia as not coping well with local rainstorms, which can overtop or wash out small field structures [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1652_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1139_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without stated reasoning or damage records, and the Ugandan planting-pit compiler rates coping as good [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1587_2013_local_rainstorm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge zaï or tassa planting pits and contour bunds in Niger and conservation tillage with the Magoye ripper in Zambia not to cope well with general river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1219_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1652_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1139_2013_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: These are three practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets, with no observed loss or failure data. Pits, bunds and ripper tillage are field-level practices, so a not-well rating describes exposure of the treated fields to floodwater rather than damage to a built structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge zaï or tassa planting pits and contour bunds in Niger and planting pits in Uganda to cope well with local windstorms; no unit describes how wind would damage them [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1219_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1652_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1587_2013_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: These are three practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets with no observed damage data. Pits and bunds are field-level practices, so the ratings describe exposure of the treated fields rather than damage to a built structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The proximity of zai pits on crusted, degraded soil raises the chances of seed germination and dispersal, so herbaceous and woody species recolonise formerly bare land in Burkina Faso [ev_biodiversity_outcome_roose93_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_zoug14_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_kabo04_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Burkina Faso evidence is descriptive, without an untreated comparison, and partly the same observation cited more than once. The only rating, a WOCAT compiler judgement for the Magoye ripper in Zambia, puts animal diversity unchanged, and that conservation-tillage sheet is a loose fit for an in-situ water-harvesting family [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1139_2013_animal_diversity].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for planting pits and stone lines, zai or tassa pits and contour bunds in Niger and planting pits in Uganda rate soil organic matter increased, and the Magoye ripper compiler in Zambia attributes slight biomass and organic matter gains to less soil disturbance [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1100_2011_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1219_2014_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1652_2014_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1587_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1139_2013_biomass_above_ground_C]. In the literature, zai fields in Burkina Faso treated for several years had higher organic matter and trenches combined with vegetation raised soil organic carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Soil organic matter is a proxy for sequestration, and the Niger and Uganda ratings carry no compiler comment and are practitioner judgements rather than measurements. The literature is mixed: trenches in Mexico reduced soil nitrogen and carbon, and a zai trial in Burkina Faso detected no significant change in organic matter even though biomass production rose; the conservation-tillage sheet sits at the edge of this family [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose93_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits, tied furrows, deep ploughing, conservation tillage and residue mulch increase infiltration and soil water storage, so crops suffer less from dry spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Zai pits concentrate runoff into the root zone, so crops can ride out a dry spell of two to three weeks.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single expert statement from Burkina Faso, explicitly conditional on the soil having sufficient water storage capacity.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Infiltration trenches, planting pits, contour bunds and conservation or basin tillage hold rain where it falls: trenches significantly reduced plot runoff and soil loss across the reviewed mountain studies and reduced sheet erosion on degraded high-Andean soils, and WOCAT compilers for tillage and pit systems in Niger, Kenya, Zambia, Burkina Faso and South Africa rate surface runoff and soil loss as reduced [ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_3, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_968_2011_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1652_2014_soil_loss].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The runoff effect of trenches was much weaker on cropland (3.5%) than on land with natural vegetation (15%), and some studies found catchment sediment concentration rising in the first years after trenches were built [ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_2, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_3, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2]. The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings; their downstream-flooding ratings are mostly slight, the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates flood impacts as worse, and the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding]. water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Planting pits (zai, tassa), tied furrows, basin tillage and infiltration trenches capture runoff near the plants; combined with manure they let cereals be grown on degraded crusted soils, and in the 1990 drought in Niger only tassa fields produced a harvest. Tied furrows in Brazil gave higher maize yields than flat traditional planting, and WOCAT compilers for pits, contour bunds and conservation tillage in Niger, Burkina Faso, Uganda, Kenya, Zambia, the Philippines and South Africa judge crop production increased.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Much of the gain depends on manure or fertiliser added to the pits: pits alone gave an average sorghum gain of only 38 kg/ha in one study against 310 kg/ha in another, and pits without manure did not raise yields significantly in a Burkina Faso trial. water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Zai pits, planting pits, contour bunds and reduced or ripper tillage raise and stabilise yields in dry years: compilers describe planting pits in Uganda keeping banana stands fruiting through drought and raising monthly harvests for sale, composting with planting pits in Burkina Faso raising farm income several times in dry years, and the Magoye ripper in Zambia improving yields and tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_959_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income]. water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: These are practitioner ratings without stated reasoning, and the Philippine conservation-tillage compiler rates wind velocity as unchanged [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1021_2011_wind_velocity]. water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry period, giving households basic drinking and cooking water near the home, cutting the time spent fetching water and postponing or avoiding the shortages that send families to water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. In a survey of beneficiary families, 57.8% said the cistern fully met drinking, cooking and personal hygiene needs, and the WOCAT compiler for a rooftop tank system in Uganda rates water quantity and availability as improved [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_quantity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit is set by storage per person: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families named the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. In great multi-year droughts the cisterns run dry and households fall back on water trucks, which records no benefit at that point rather than damage to the tank [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3]. The survey used recall with no control group, the other Brazilian units are implementer or author statements, and the Ugandan units are practitioner ratings; all describe domestic water access as a component proxy, not crop or livestock losses [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry season, but in great multi-year droughts they run dry and households fall back on water trucks, leaving them very vulnerable [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single expert statement from a Brazilian programme account, upper-middle-income and adjacent to the target; it records no drought benefit once storage is exhausted, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the tank, and says nothing about shorter droughts.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The pooled cost is the average construction cost of a roof rainwater-harvesting tank under the Himachal Pradesh mid-Himalayan watershed project in India, reported per structure from the project's output table.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single lender completion report, self-reported from physical and financial monitoring; the figure is a nominal rupee average over the project years converted at one exchange rate, so it indicates the order of cost of a household tank rather than a transferable unit rate.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop tanks capture part of the rain falling on roofs; the WOCAT compiler for a rooftop system with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda rates surface runoff and downstream flooding as reduced [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1595_2013_surface_runoff, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1595_2013_downstream_flooding].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both sheets are practitioner ratings, and the Nepal compiler rates downstream flooding as unchanged because only a little portion of rainfall is trapped from the roof [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_flooding].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop systems trap part of the rainfall from roofs, and the compiler for Rubagano rooftop harvesting with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda judged downstream flooding slightly reduced.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner judgements from technology sheets; the Nepal compiler rated the effect neutral because only a little rainfall is trapped from the roof, so any flood benefit is marginal.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler's rating on the WOCAT sheet for the Rubagano rooftop rainwater harvesting system with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda, which records crop production as increased; the sheet gives no comment on how the stored roof water reaches crops [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1595_2013_crop_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a practitioner judgement from a documented technology sheet, not a measured yield, and no literature unit supports it; whether the rating holds beyond this single Ugandan technology is untested [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1595_2013_crop_production].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Ugandan Rubagano rooftop system's WOCAT sheet rates farm income and food self-sufficiency as increased [ev_household_income_wocat_1595_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1595_2013_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In Brazil, domestic cisterns fully met family drinking and household needs for many households and improved quality of life and health, but did not influence income [ev_household_income_silva09_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The signals point in different directions: a Brazilian household survey from an upper-middle-income setting finds no income effect, while the Ugandan input is a single compiler's ratings that also record the risk of production failure as unchanged [ev_household_income_silva09_3, ev_food_security_wocat_1595_2013_risk_of_production_failure]. Neither source measures income change, and the Brazilian null concerns cash income rather than other welfare outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Capturing roof runoff in a tank keeps it off the ground around the homestead: the Ugandan Rubagano sheet rates surface runoff as reduced, and the Nepali compiler notes less eroded material from the courtyard [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1595_2013_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings, and the Nepali sheet rates downstream siltation unchanged despite its comment, so any effect is confined to the homestead and is not measured [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation]. Runoff reduction and sediment retention enter only as component proxies for soil erosion.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Nepali rooftop rainwater harvesting sheet rates downstream siltation unchanged, while its compiler notes less eroded material from the courtyard [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating of downstream siltation, a component proxy; it says nothing about the quality of the stored water itself [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns store rainwater beside the house, giving households basic drinking and cooking water through the dry season, sharply reducing time spent fetching water and dependence on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. The Ugandan Rubagano sheet rates water quantity as greatly increased [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_quantity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units come from cistern programmes in Brazil (upper-middle income), largely programme authors and household surveys. A standard cistern covers basic needs only for small households, larger families remain dependent on water trucks, and most households still use other sources as their main supply [ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. The Ugandan sheet rates overall water availability only slightly improved [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Subsurface dams in semi-arid Brazil tended to dry out during a year without rain, and small manually built dams do not withstand long droughts, limiting production through dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. WOCAT compilers rate check dams in China, Nepal and India and sand dams in Kenya as coping well with drought, and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1455_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1537_2012_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_7777_2026_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Brazilian units describe storage exhaustion rather than structural damage, and the rest are practitioner ratings of coping without observed failure data [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge check dams in Tunisia, China and India, sand dams in Kenya and fascine check dams in Madagascar to cope well with local rainstorms, and gully-plugging check dams in Nepal not to cope well; a masonry check dam in Ethiopia is judged to cope well with landslides, while check dams in India and gabion structures in Somalia are judged to cope moderately with landslides or storms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1400_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6716_2023_landslide, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5210_2019_landslide, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets without observed damage or failure rates. These are built structures in gullies and channels, so the ratings bear on the works themselves rather than on fields.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for stone check walls and check dams in India rates the technology as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating with no observed damage or stated reasoning [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia still failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, and when peak flows break check dams the stored sediment is released rapidly [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers rate gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and check-dam ponds in Ethiopia as not coping well with floods and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Other compilers rate check dams in Tunisia, China and India and sand dams in Kenya as coping well, and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia as coping very well with flash floods, so sensitivity varies with construction [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1400_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood]. The check-dam failure evidence is cited from other studies, the sediment-release statement comes from a USA study, the Ghana finding gives no count of dams lost, and the ratings are practitioner judgements [ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_damage_veno12_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rates the technology as coping moderately with heatwaves [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating with no stated reason or observed damage [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, and Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate check dams in China and Nepal and sand dams in Kenya as coping well with local windstorms and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately, while fascine (vegetative) check dams in Madagascar are rated as not coping well with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1455_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1537_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage; the Madagascar sheet alone rates tropical storms, and it concerns a vegetative structure rather than stone or concrete [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge that water stored by runoff structures supports plant growth and habitat: on-farm ponds in Cambodia make water available for plants, sand dams in Kenya rejuvenate riverine ecologies and enable indigenous tree planting, and gabions and rock check dams in Somalia improved soil moisture, reduced erosion and restored vegetation, creating habitat for livestock and small wildlife [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2844_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1537_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_habitat_diversity]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1].
