water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Apart from the Ghana user-perception statement, all units are compiler ratings from technology sheets in Kenya, Cambodia, Ethiopia and Somalia, mostly rated as slight change and several from the same sheet; the Ethiopian check-dam comment gives no mechanism, and no unit measures species or habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6716_2023_plant_diversity].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge that gabions and rock check dams in Somalia increase vegetation, above-ground biomass and soil organic matter through vegetation recovery and sediment accumulation, that a haffir in Somalia does so as vegetation cover regenerates, that tree cover at a masonry check dam in Ethiopia reduces emissions over time, and that tree nurseries enabled by sand dams in Kenya store carbon and reduce deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7778_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7777_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_6716_2023_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1537_2012_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, all rated slight, with no measured carbon; biomass, soil organic matter and avoided-emission ratings are proxies for sequestration, and several units come from the same Somali sheet.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The unit reports how often rehabilitated small dams in Ghana came in under per-irrigated-hectare cost thresholds, comparing the government irrigation authority with donor and NGO implementers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a cost distribution by implementer for reservoir rehabilitation, not a measured cost reduction from water harvesting; treat it as context on rehabilitation cost variability.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Runoff-fed storage holds water into the dry season: Kenyan communities with a sand dam had water 2.5 months longer than those relying on the riverbed, subsurface dams in Brazil raised well levels that households used when other sources dried up, production cisterns kept livestock watered, and pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduced farming risk in irregular years [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. WOCAT compilers for check dams, sand dams, haffirs and on-farm ponds in India, Kenya, Tunisia, Ethiopia, Somalia and Cambodia rate water quantity, soil moisture and drought impacts as improved, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5210_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1400_2011_water_quantity, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Storage capacity limits the effect: at least 67% of 30 Kenyan sand dams could not supply even one household through the whole dry season, 57% of assessed dams would serve their reported users only as a sole source, and Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year, small ones not withstanding long dry spells, a benefit shortfall rather than damage [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count, and the Brazilian pond statement an institutional self-assessment, while most units are WOCAT practitioner ratings; the Indian farm-pond sheet rates soil moisture as unchanged and Ethiopian compilers say off-site effects of recently built dams still need assessment [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1474_2011_soil_moisture, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6716_2023_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Ponds, cisterns and check dams store runoff for use in dry periods: runoff ponds in semi-arid Brazil supply supplemental irrigation during dry spells, cisterns in China are reported to mitigate frequent droughts, and the compiler of a Cambodian on-farm pond sheet states the pond provides enough water even during drought. WOCAT compilers for check dams and gully works in India, Ethiopia and Somalia likewise judge drought impacts reduced, the Somali sheet citing better soil moisture retention and infiltration.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most of the pool is practitioner judgements and assertions without drought-loss metrics: an expert account from Brazil, a lender evaluation in China, and a review that counts how often small-reservoir studies cite improved drought resilience; none measures avoided losses. Subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells, which records no benefit when storage is exhausted rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The pooled costs are average construction costs of village ponds or tanks per structure and of dry-stone drainage-line check dams per cubic metre of structure, from the output table of the Himachal Pradesh mid-Himalayan watershed project in India.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One lender completion report, self-reported from project monitoring, in nominal rupees converted at a single exchange rate; the per-cubic-metre figure is per cubic metre of masonry built, not per cubic metre of water stored, so it is not comparable with storage-cost figures and the cost class should be read with that denominator in mind.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for stone check walls and check dams in India rates fire risk as reduced, but the sheet gives no explanation of how the structures do this [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The row rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated mechanism and no measurement, so the class reflects one compiler's judgement for one Indian technology [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, check dams, sand dams and haffirs store or slow runoff: hill reservoirs in the Merguellil basin in Tunisia were modelled to reduce outlet flows by 13%, users of small reservoirs in northern Ghana list limiting rainy-season floods among their benefits, and WOCAT compilers for check dams in China, Tunisia, Ethiopia, India, Nicaragua and Somalia and for sand dams in Kenya rate surface runoff, soil loss and downstream flooding as reduced [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1400_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Tunisian figure is modelled, the Ghana finding is user perception, and the WOCAT units are practitioner ratings, so no unit measures a flood reduction directly [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. Size and siting can reverse the effect: larger sand dams increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage, check dams caused channel incision downstream at 81% of surveyed dams in a Spanish catchment, and the Indian farm-pond sheet rates soil loss and downstream flooding as unchanged [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, sand dams and haffirs slow runoff, retain sediment and buffer peak flows, which WOCAT compilers in Tunisia, China, Kenya, Ethiopia, Nicaragua, Syria and Somalia judge to reduce downstream flooding; in Kenya a series of sand dams creates a buffer that reduces flooding downstream, and users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Nearly all units are practitioner judgements or user perceptions, not measurements. A review notes larger sand dams raise flooding, erosion and seepage risk, a farm pond in India was rated neutral, and the Somali gully-works sheet records downstream flooding with a negative value although its comment describes reduced flooding, so that unit's sign is likely a scale artefact.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, small reservoirs, subsurface dams, farm ponds, check dams and haffirs store runoff that farmers use to irrigate more land and take a second or dry-season crop, while sediment trapped behind check dams can be planted with fodder; in Kenya sand-dam water lets farmers irrigate more crops and raise production, and in Brazil soil management in subsurface dams raised crop productivity [ev_crop_yield_ritc21_1, ev_crop_yield_brito07_5, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1474_2011_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_2844_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6716_2023_fodder_production]. WOCAT compilers in Somalia describe reliable irrigation from a haffir improving tomato and watermelon, grasses regenerating around the dam, and better water and fodder raising animal production [ev_crop_yield_wocat_7777_2026_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_7777_2026_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_7777_2026_animal_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT technology sheets, and the literature units are largely reviews citing earlier studies, an expert's personal communication on livestock, and Brazilian case accounts from an upper-middle-income setting [ev_crop_yield_ritc21_1, ev_livestock_productivity_veno12_1, ev_crop_yield_cirilo03_4]. A Brazilian subsurface dam produced no harvest in a year of adverse weather, and an Indian farm-pond sheet rates fodder production unchanged; fodder and livestock outcomes enter only as components of the production gap [ev_crop_yield_brito07_6, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1474_2011_fodder_production].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income and lean-season food security [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]. WOCAT compilers add that farm ponds in Cambodia keep enough irrigation water through drought, gully check dams in Ethiopia free rangeland for grazing, and gully rehabilitation in Somalia raised crop and livestock productivity [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts, and practitioner ratings make up a large share of the pool [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. Compilers rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and an Indian subsistence farm pond as leaving farm income unchanged; Kenyan sand dams are embedded in a wider food-security programme [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines and gully plugs trap sediment in gullies and channels, reducing catchment sediment export, and hill reservoirs reduce outlet flows [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4]. WOCAT compilers describe masonry check dams in Ethiopia slowing runoff so soil accumulates upstream, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia cutting runoff speed and gully expansion, and vegetative check dams in Madagascar reducing siltation of downstream rice fields [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7778_2026_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6478_2022_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings; the pooled sediment figures come from a single check-dam synthesis, so the independent literature base is narrow [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_3]. Check dams can cause downstream channel incision through the clear-water effect (documented in Spain, a high-income setting), gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising to keep working, an Indian sheet rates soil loss unchanged, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that the visible siltation held back has not been quantified [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines and gully plugs store sediment in channels, reducing catchment sediment yield and the topsoil washed downstream [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate downstream siltation as reduced, from stem-cutting check dams in Nicaragua and stone check walls in India to gabions and check dams in Somalia that trap sediment upstream of fields and water bodies, and gully plugs in Nepal that cut siltation into an irrigation canal [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1719_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5210_2019_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1493_2011_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, and most units are practitioner ratings; the literature magnitudes come from a single check-dam synthesis, and gabions in Morocco have filled up and need raising to keep trapping sediment [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. Sheets for olive runoff furrows in Syria, a gabion check dam in Tunisia and check-dam ponds in Ethiopia rate only a slight reduction [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1005_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1400_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1547_2012_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams, ponds and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up. WOCAT compilers for gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dam ponds and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia, sand dams in Kenya, stone check walls in India, on-farm ponds in Cambodia and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia judge them to improve water harvesting, quantity or availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1400_2011_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1547_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_harvesting_collection_of_water].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The groundwater effect of sand dams is limited in space and time, many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. Several literature units are review citations or vote counts, the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that off-site impacts of the recently built check dam still need assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6716_2023_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for gully plugging with check dams in Nepal, stone check walls and check dams in India and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no stated reasoning or measurement, and the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate drainage as unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for stone check walls and check dams in India and for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced, the Somali compiler noting the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff; the Syrian furrow-harvesting compiler rates wind velocity as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1005_2011_wind_velocity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no measurement, and the storm ratings concern rain-storm runoff damage rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with drought, and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1013_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1333_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6715_2023_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no observed damage data; spate systems depend on flood flows, so drought is more likely to cut their water supply than to damage the structures.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local rainstorms, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately, and marab agriculture in Jordan as coping very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1333_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6715_2023_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Large floods could wash out traditional spate diversion structures in Yemen, making it hard to get floodwater onto the land, and the WOCAT compiler for jessour in Tunisia rates them as not coping well with river floods [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements, and compilers for water spreading in Sudan and spate irrigation in Eritrea rate coping as good, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as moderate and marab agriculture in Jordan as very good [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1292_2015_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1333_2010_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6715_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood]. All ratings are practitioner judgements without damage records.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1013_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1333_2010_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of a WOCAT sheet on water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judged habitat and plant diversity slightly increased; no mechanism is described.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single technology sheet supplies all units and it rated animal diversity unchanged; these are practitioner judgements, not measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets for marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan, water spreading in Sudan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate soil organic matter increased under these flood-spreading systems, and the Ethiopian sheet also rates emissions reduced; the sheets give no mechanism for these ratings.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements with no compiler comment, not measurements; the Jordan sheet rates the gain strongly while the Sudan and Ethiopia sheets rate it as slight, and soil organic matter and emission ratings stand in for sequestration.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The pooled cost is the average investment cost of spate systems under a World Bank groundwater and soil conservation project in Yemen, reported at USD 800-1200 per hectare, with farmers expected to contribute a 15-20% share, about USD 150-200 per hectare.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single lender completion-report figure from a low-income context, with no cost breakdown and no restoration outcome attached, so it describes investment cost per hectare of spate system rather than cost per hectare restored; the report itself calls the farmer contribution comparatively high.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading systems (spate irrigation, water-spreading weirs, jessour and marab floodplain agriculture) slow and spread flood runoff over fields so it soaks in, and WOCAT compilers in Eritrea, Ethiopia, Sudan, Tunisia and Jordan rate soil moisture and water availability as improved and drought impacts as reduced [ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1333_2010_soil_moisture, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_6715_2023_soil_moisture, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1013_2011_water_availability, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a WOCAT compiler rating rather than a measured result, and most rate soil moisture or water quantity as component proxies for drought impact. The Sudan water-spreading sheet rates water availability as unchanged, and the Ethiopian compiler says the structure is too recent to judge off-site effects [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets on marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge drought impacts reduced, without describing the mechanism.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner judgements from technology sheets, with no measurement; the Jordan sheet comes from an upper-middle-income context adjacent to the target.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and diversion structures, water-spreading weirs, jessour and marab floodplain systems slow and spread flood flows across fields: Bank reporting from Yemen says spate and diversion structures reduce soil erosion, control floods and reduce wadi-bank damage, and WOCAT compilers in Tunisia, Jordan, Ethiopia and Sudan rate surface runoff, soil loss and downstream flooding as reduced, the Ethiopian compiler noting the weirs cut the speed and volume of downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen statements are a Bank completion report, one resting on farmers' interviews, and the remaining units are WOCAT practitioner ratings; none measures flood peaks or damage [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Jessour, water spreading, marab floodplain systems and water-spreading weirs reduce the speed and volume of downstream flooding, as the Ethiopian weir compiler states, and the Yemen completion report says spate and diversion structures control floods and distribute water more evenly to downstream farmers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The pool is practitioner judgements from technology sheets in Tunisia, Sudan, Jordan and Ethiopia plus a lender self-reported assertion from Yemen; none measures flood peaks or volumes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Jessour in Tunisia, water spreading in Sudan, spate irrigation in Eritrea, marab floodplain farming in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia divert and spread floodwater over fields as spate or supplementary irrigation, and compilers rate crop and fodder production as increased [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1013_2011_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1333_2010_crop_production]. Much of the gain is fed to livestock: crops in the Jordan marab are used as fodder, crop residues in Eritrea feed animals, and Ethiopian compilers link fodder gains to the soil and moisture conserved behind the structure [ev_crop_yield_wocat_5770_2020_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_fodder_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT technology sheet; there is no literature measurement in this cell. The Ethiopian rating is stated as the expert's conviction, and the Sudan rating is relative to nothing being grown otherwise, so the scale of the gain is a counterfactual judgement rather than a yield comparison [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1292_2015_crop_production].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets for jessour in Tunisia, spate irrigation in Eritrea, water spreading in Sudan, marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge these floodwater-diverting systems to have improved food self-sufficiency and increased farm income, and those that rate it judge the risk of production failure to have decreased. The Ethiopian compiler attributes this to improved crop resilience from better soil moisture [ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner judgement from a documented technology sheet, not a household survey or measured income change, and poverty is reached only through food-security and farm-income proxies. The pool is five sheets, and the Jordanian sheet comes from an upper-middle-income setting.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading structures control flood flows on the land: in Yemen spate development reduces damage to wadi banks and lets areas re-green, and Ethiopian compilers say the physical barriers stop soil and water loss [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_soil_loss]. Sheets for jessour in Tunisia, marab farming in Jordan and water spreading in Sudan rate soil loss, surface runoff or downstream siltation as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1013_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1292_2015_surface_runoff].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The only literature unit is a farmer-perception figure in a lender completion report from Yemen [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; the rest are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and the Jordan siltation comment states a desired rather than observed outcome [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation]. Runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sheets for jessour in Tunisia, marab floodplain farming in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate downstream siltation as reduced, as floodwater and its sediment are spread and held on the fields [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1013_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation, a component proxy for water quality, and the Jordan comment states reduced siltation as a desired rather than an observed outcome [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading systems divert floodwater onto fields: WOCAT compilers for jessour in Tunisia, spate irrigation in Eritrea, water spreading in Sudan, marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge them to improve water harvesting, and the Ethiopian compiler credits the weirs with a positive contribution to groundwater in adjacent farms [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. In Yemen, groundwater tables downstream of spate and conservation structures were maintained or increased, and spate beneficiaries report considerably increased groundwater levels [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen evidence is a completion-report comment and focus-group reports, so it is self-reported, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements. The Sudan compiler judges no change in water availability, and the Ethiopian compiler notes the weirs are too recent to judge off-site impacts [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without stated reasoning or measurement, from technologies built to spread floodwater over fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rates wind velocity as reduced [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_6715_2023_wind_velocity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same compiler rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as unchanged, and both units are practitioner ratings from one technology sheet [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate terraces, stone lines and stone bunds in China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Uganda, Niger, Haiti and Tunisia as coping well with drought, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1522_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1553_2012_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6610_2022_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_4284_2018_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings of coping, with no observed damage or failure data.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger as not coping well with local rainstorms, while terraces and stone lines in China, Yemen, Uganda, Haiti and Tunisia are rated as coping well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6610_2022_landslide].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage; compilers for bench terraces in Haiti, Thailand and Bangladesh rate coping with landslides, rainstorms or hailstorms as very good, and vegetated stone bunds in Burkina Faso as moderate [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_landslide, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6729_2023_local_thunderstorm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh rates them as coping moderately with forest fire and well with land fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units come from one technology sheet and are practitioner ratings without observed damage.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Banquettes lack the capacity to absorb runoff from erosive rains and overflow, diversion channels fill with eroded soil and overflow in the heaviest storms, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. WOCAT compilers judge radical terraces in Rwanda and contour stone bunds in Niger not to cope well with river floods, while stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, stone lines in Tunisia and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan are judged to cope well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1553_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6610_2022_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7553_2025_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Failure is tied to maintenance and setting: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. The literature hazards are erosive rains, torrential rain and mass movements mapped to flood and come as expert and modelled statements without failure rates, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than records of damage [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger as coping well with local windstorms, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti as coping well with tropical storms, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with both [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1573_2013_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1616_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_3223_2017_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage, and the progressive bench terrace in China is rated as not coping well with local windstorms, with no reason given [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for contour stone bunds in Bhutan links higher plant diversity to the soil becoming suitable for more diverse crops, and the compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh expects soil flora and fauna to find a suitable environment once the planned cropping system is established [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4284_2018_animal_diversity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings from technology sheets, not measurements; the Bhutan rating describes crop diversity and the Bangladesh rating an anticipated rather than observed change, so neither speaks to wild species.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and stone lines are rated by their compilers as building below-ground soil organic matter on treated land, through an expanding root system under orchard terraces and retained soil behind stone lines [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1589_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6610_2022_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]; one bench-terrace sheet also rates emissions as reduced because the crops of a more intensive rotation absorb carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_4284_2018_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a technology sheet, not a measured carbon stock; the stone-bund sheet says organic matter falls at the top of the terrace and rises at the bottom, a redistribution within the field rather than a net gain [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6891_2023_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C], and the bench-terrace rationale is higher cropping intensity, which is not long-term storage [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4284_2018_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The single figure is the cost of rehabilitating some pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru, a heavy earth- and stone-moving intervention.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One historical assessment from an upper-middle-income Andean context, cited secondhand; it is not representative of new terrace construction in LIC/LMIC settings and carries no currency-year adjustment.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and stone lines slow runoff and promote infiltration, raising soil moisture; when rainfall is erratic stone bunds conserve moisture and ease crop water stress during dry spells, and crops behind stone bunds could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Leveled fields on China's Loess Plateau increased moisture retention and broad bench terraces in semi-arid China held up to 22% more moisture than vegetated slopes, and WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone bunds in Niger, Tunisia, Bhutan, Ethiopia, Yemen, Peru, Haiti, Uzbekistan and other countries rate soil moisture as improved and drought impacts as reduced [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2, ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_2, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1616_2014_soil_moisture, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield benefit in the driest year and so did not reduce famine risk then, which bounds the cited dry-year gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The Loess Plateau result has no control, the Indian result is farmer perception, the Rwandan resilience finding comes from a bundled land-husbandry package, and most units are WOCAT practitioner ratings of soil moisture, a component proxy; the Haiti compiler states the drought effect has not yet been measured [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2, ev_soil_water_retention_iegind11_9, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone lines capture and infiltrate more water so the land is less susceptible to drought, as the compiler for gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan puts it; compilers for terraces in Haiti and Bangladesh and stone lines in Tunisia also judge drought impacts reduced, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Haiti compiler notes the impact has not yet been measured; the Rwanda result is an impact evaluation against controls reported second-hand in a completion report, without a magnitude or outcome metric.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little fuel, and the WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh rates fire risk as reduced [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The terrace statement is an expert estimate its authors say has no experimental basis on terraces, and the Bangladesh unit is a practitioner rating with no stated reasoning [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk]. The effect depends on residues being removed by grazing.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and banquettes slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces cut mean runoff by 50 to 98% and flood peaks on small mountain plots, a global study of 105 cases finds terraces on average 2.5 times more effective than slopes at reducing runoff, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment cut runoff volume by 50% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_runoff_reduction_willem21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2]. WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone bunds in Rwanda, China, Tunisia, Yemen, Peru, Haiti, Uzbekistan and other countries rate runoff, soil loss and downstream flooding as reduced, and compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand are credited with limiting damage from landslides and flood [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_flooding, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1522_2010_surface_runoff, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they doubled the runoff coefficient, raised peak discharges and increased gully and bank erosion, and ditches with a downslope bank accelerate runoff and concentration time [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Abandoned terraces increase erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or never maintained, catchment-level peak-flow evidence is scarce, and most units, including the WOCAT practitioner ratings, are runoff or soil-loss proxies for flood impact [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1]. The Rwanda sediment figures and the Uttarakhand claim are Bank self-reports, and the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, stone lines and contour stone bunds detain and spread runoff on slopes, lowering peak discharges and making flows last longer after rain; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50%, and WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone lines in many countries judge downstream flooding reduced, the Tunisian stone-lines sheet citing lower peak flows during heavy rainfall.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes raised peak discharges, and breached dikes risk gullying, so design decides the sign. Catchment-scale evidence is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian treatment also included rangeland closure, the Uttarakhand flood-mitigation claim is lender self-reported, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces, fanya juu and contour stone bunds or lines level slopes and slow runoff so more water and soil stay on the field; yields of maize, barley, millet and sorghum rose on terraced or bunded land, especially in dry years. Stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% in Burkina Faso and by about 142% with compost, and millet yields in Niger rose by more than 40% up to 15 years after the bunds were built [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. WOCAT compilers add that stone lines in Tunisia protect farmland from degradation, contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area as stones are removed, and Gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan turn unproductive land productive [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6610_2022_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_6891_2023_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_7553_2025_crop_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Several literature figures are lender self-reports (Rwanda before/after yields, Indian with/without models bundled with crop packages); the Rwanda value-of-harvest gain is from an independent DIME evaluation, and the Burkina Faso and Niger gains are cited from earlier studies, the largest bundled with compost [ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4]. Diversion banquettes in Niger reduced yields, progressive terraces on poor soils in Rwanda gave no yield increase, bench terraces need heavy fertility restoration before yields rise, and a Haitian compiler notes that on very degraded land farmers must wait for the soil to recover [ev_crop_yield_heusch95_1, ev_crop_yield_roose06_3, ev_crop_yield_roose94_4, ev_crop_yield_wocat_3223_2017_crop_production]. Most pooled units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets rather than measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing raises yields and enables higher-value crops on former hillsides, which drives positive modelled returns per hectare and improved food consumption in project households; terrace investments are judged to pay off over long lifetimes, mainly where they carry high-value crops such as vegetables [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_food_security_rwa18_5, ev_economic_return_willem21_1, ev_economic_return_fao13c_1]. WOCAT compilers report continuous income from tea on bench terraces in Thailand, a per-hectare income gain from progressive bench terraces in China, contour stone bunds in Bhutan meeting household maize demand, and Gradoni terraces in Uzbekistan improving drought resilience [ev_household_income_wocat_4281_2018_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1522_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_6891_2023_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_7553_2025_risk_of_production_failure].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets; the literature returns are lender crop-budget models for Rwanda and India, and the food-security gain is an independent DIME evaluation [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_household_income_utk22_9, ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. A review reports terraces reducing net crop income in Ethiopia and banquette profitability in Niger was close to nil; compilers record no change in food security for vetiver terraces in Haiti, where farmers must wait for degraded soil to recover, and on sheets from Rwanda [ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_heusch95_1, ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Food security, income and returns are proxies for poverty.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers rate soil loss and runoff as reduced on terraces from China to Uzbekistan, noting that stone lines in Tunisia cut runoff by 50% and that Gradoni terraces trap soil eroded from the inter-spaces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_6610_2022_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1522_2010_surface_runoff].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and retaining walls hold soil on slopes, which an evaluation in Morocco expects to reduce siltation of downstream rivers and dam storage [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers rate downstream siltation as reduced for radical terraces in Rwanda, bench terraces in Yemen and Bangladesh, stone lines in Uganda and Tunisia, contour stone bunds in Niger and vetiver terraces in Haiti [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1560_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1616_2014_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Morocco unit is an evaluator assertion and the rest are practitioner ratings; nothing on water quality or sediment is measured, and siltation is a component proxy [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. The Gradoni terrace sheet for Uzbekistan rates only a slight reduction [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7553_2025_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces, stone lines and contour ridges retain rainfall on slopes so part of it infiltrates and recharges groundwater [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. WOCAT compilers judge bench terraces in Yemen, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, contour stone bunds in Niger and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan to improve water harvesting, and radical terraces in Rwanda, vetiver terraces in Haiti, stone lines in Tunisia and semi-circular stone bunds in Ethiopia to improve water quantity or availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1560_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The recharge evidence is a modelling study (Morocco) and an estimate from the Mandara mountains (Cameroon), the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and catchment modelling in Peru found no difference in crop water distribution with partial terracing [ev_water_regulation_willem21_1]. Abandoned or degraded terraces worsen water regulation [ev_water_regulation_willem21_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone bunds hold runoff in the field, and in wet years this can waterlog parts of the field and harm crop production; millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. WOCAT compilers for terraces in Peru, Yemen and Cabo Verde instead rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1560_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The harm comes from cited statements from Burkina Faso that apply only to wet years or very wet months and give no magnitude, while the opposing units are practitioner ratings for bench and stone-wall terraces rather than stone bunds, so the two sides may describe different structures [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for radical terraces in Rwanda, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti and stone lines in Tunisia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced, and compilers for contour stone bunds in Niger and vegetated stone bunds in Burkina Faso rate wind velocity as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1616_2014_wind_velocity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings, the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured, and the Cabo Verde stone-wall terrace sheet rates wind velocity as unchanged [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1573_2013_wind_velocity].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines, terraces and bunds trap sediment that would otherwise reach streams, canals and reservoirs, lowering catchment sediment export and downstream siltation [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers describe gabion walls and check dams in Somalia trapping sediment upstream and reducing siltation of downstream fields and water bodies, and vegetative check dams in Madagascar reducing siltation of downstream rice fields [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6478_2022_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: Water quality is inferred entirely from sediment retention, a component proxy; nothing is measured on nutrients or water chemistry, and most units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation from WOCAT sheets. Much of the literature magnitude is from a single check-dam synthesis, the China figure is a modelled programme estimate, and gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. Sheets from Nepal and Niger rate siltation unchanged, the Zambian tillage sheet expects a benefit only at large scale, and the Ethiopian compiler notes the trapped sediment has not been quantified [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Pits, bunds, terraces, trenches and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge; cisterns, sand dams and subsurface dams store water close to homes, cutting time spent fetching water and dependence on water tankers through the dry season. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix recharge, spring discharge and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger, and Ethiopian compilers note that off-site effects of recently built structures are yet to be assessed [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. Groundwater gains are often local and short-lived, can be wiped out by increased pumping, and year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season, domestic cisterns cover basic needs only for small households, and trenches had little effect on baseflow or infiltration [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_regulation_locat20_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: domestic and production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil give households basic drinking water, keep livestock watered when clay tanks are dry and reduce dependence on water trucks, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. Stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale raise groundwater levels, and in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to runoff control and better infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, only 19.1% of surveyed families used the cistern as their main source, and 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. In Burkina Faso the number of wells with year-round water had not increased significantly since soil and water conservation began, and most units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from upper-middle-income Brazil rather than the low-income target [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, pits, bunds, terraces and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge, and sand dams store water that extends the months of water access. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, rooftop tanks, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Many literature units are lender-reported or community perceptions and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability]. Groundwater gains in India could be wiped out by increased pumping, year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso, and many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, domestic and production cisterns and subsurface dams store rain for the dry season, giving households basic drinking water, keeping livestock watered and reducing dependence on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. A few catchment studies of trenches observe reduced quick runoff or increased aquifer recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Storage limits the benefit: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families used the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. Catchment effects are weak or unproven: recharge gains cannot be generalised, trenches have little effect on baseflow and no significant effect on infiltration rates, terracing 20% of cropland made no difference in a Peruvian catchment model, and abandoned terraces can harm water regulation [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1, ev_water_regulation_locat20_1, ev_soil_permeability_locat20_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Practices that hold water in the field can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger, conservation tillage in Kenya and the Philippines also rate drainage of excess water as worse, while compilers for terraces, check dams, water-spreading weirs and other works in Peru, Nepal, India, Yemen, Ethiopia, Cabo Verde and Jordan rate it as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The pool is split: the literature units that show harm are tied to wet years or high-rainfall zones and give no magnitude or share of field affected, while more of the units, all WOCAT practitioner ratings, report better drainage; the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and sorghum in zaï pits in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields; WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya also rate drainage of excess water as worse [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage]. Compilers for check dams in Nepal and India, bench terraces in Yemen, water-spreading weirs and check dams in Ethiopia, ripper tillage in Zambia and composted planting pits in Burkina Faso rate drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_959_2010_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Harm appears in wet years or high-rainfall zones and is not quantified, and the units that report it are cited statements or an unpublished observation, while the opposing units are practitioner ratings; the Indian farm-pond sheet rates drainage as unchanged [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The direction depends on whether a practice ponds water in the field or channels it away.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for the rehabilitation of ancient terraces in Peru, reinforced stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no measurement; the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates drainage as worse and the Chinese check-dam sheet rates it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced for terraces in Rwanda and Haiti, stone lines in Tunisia, check walls and check dams in India, Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan and gabions with rock check dams in Somalia, the Somali compiler noting the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Compilers for pits, bunds and trenches in Niger and Burkina Faso, furrow harvesting in Syria and weirs in Ethiopia rate wind velocity as reduced, the Burkina Faso compiler crediting the many growing trees [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1528_2012_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1616_2014_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1219_2014_wind_velocity].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: Every unit is a WOCAT practitioner rating with no measurement, and the storm ratings concern rain-storm damage more than wind; the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Compilers in Ethiopia, the Philippines and Cabo Verde rate storm impacts or wind velocity as unchanged [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1021_2011_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1573_2013_wind_velocity].

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reasoning, and the compilers for conservation tillage in the Philippines and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde rate wind velocity as unchanged [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1021_2011_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1573_2013_wind_velocity].
